title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval & Guardrails
summary: Weekly POC sync to review quality/regression results from last week's prompt tuning runs, discuss guardrail false positives, and align on next benchmark steps. Customer raised SSO/KMS questions and requested Dedicated pricing and security docs.
next_steps: Lina - send updated prompt set and scoring spreadsheet (link) by 2025-04-24
Raj - provision benchmark harness and run 3x throughput/latency tests on Tuesday 2025-04-29
Priya - confirm encryption/KMS requirements and provide SSO metadata by 2025-04-29
Lina - share Dedicated pricing and SLA summary by 2025-04-25
action_items: Lina - deliver prompt tuning results + example regressions (2025-04-24)
Raj - add auto-regression alerts to the eval dashboard and share read-only link (2025-04-28)
Jenna - provide canonical evaluation queries and scoring rubric (2025-04-24)
Priya - send security questionnaire answers & contact for compliance (2025-04-27)
transcript:
[00:00] Lina Torres: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, is this time still good?
[00:06] Jenna Morris: Yep all good, thanks Lina.
[00:09] Raj Patel: Hey, morning. We've got the weekly quality eval to run through. I pulled the prompt sets you sent last week and the scoring runs.
[00:17] Carlos Vega: Great, we're mostly here to see regressions and verify the guardrails arent flagging too much sensitive content, and also go over perf.
[00:25] Lina Torres: Perfect. Quick agenda: results summary, regressed cases, guardrail tuning, then next bench plan. We'll call out any blockers.
[00:33] Raj Patel: Ok jumping in. So overall the weighted accuracy is up 2.8% from the baseline after the prompt re-write, but we did see a notable regression on the billing-related prompts - about a 12% drop.
[00:44] Jenna Morris: Hmm the billing prompts are high-value for us, can you show an example?
[00:49] Raj Patel: Sure, example: original prompt "What's my outstanding invoice for March" used to get structured invoice id and amount; new prompt variant sometimes returns a generic "please check billing portal" which is lower score. Transcription note: sometimes the model returns "invoice number is null" which I suspect is a tokenization/templating mismatch.
[01:07] Carlos Vega: That is concerning. We rely on the structured extraction. Are you using KV cache or some other stateful approach in the POC?
[01:15] Raj Patel: We're using prefix caching and a light KV cache; might be hitting a corner where the prompt rewrite changes the prefix so caching isn't hitting - we saw the hit rate drop from 87% to 63% on that intent. Also there might be a truncation on longer context.
[01:29] Jenna Morris: Ok can you try the previous prompt with the new guardrail layer? We have a couple of business rules that if the answer doesn't include an amount/ID it should fallback to the extraction model.
[01:40] Raj Patel: Yep we can add that. On the guardrails front, Priya, you had noted too many false positives for health-related content, can you expand?
[01:48] Priya Shah: Yeah we saw the policy classifier flagging benign clinical scheduling text as PHI. Example: "I need to reschedule my physical" flagged as sensitive. That's noisy for our UX.
[01:59] Raj Patel: (laughs) transcription glitch here, but yes that aligns. We can relax the classifier threshold for scheduling intents and add a custom allowlist for domain-specific phrases. We'll log the change into the eval dashboard.
[02:12] Sam Liu: Quick Q on latency: baseline P95 was 340ms, after some quantization profile changes it jumped to 520ms for longer sequences. Is that expected?
[02:21] Raj Patel: The quantization we tested increased compute for the long-sequence path due to fallback kernels, so latency increased. We can try an alternate quant profile or route long sequences to a different model variant to keep P95 under 400ms. That would be a routing rule change.
[02:36] Jenna Morris: What about cost — routing to a smaller model for long sequences could save cost, though we worry about quality drift.
[02:44] Lina Torres: Tradeoff as always: cost vs quality vs latency. We'll propose two policy options in the playbook doc: conservative routing (keep quality) vs hybrid routing (save cost).
[02:55] Raj Patel: Also ran the regression detector — flagged 18 query clusters as significant regressions. Most are around numeric extraction and a couple on tone/defensiveness. I've uploaded a spreadsheet with sample inputs/outputs and scoring: link: https://redwood.example/reports/acme-weekly-2025-04-22.xlsx
[03:13] Jenna Morris: Ok we'll review the spreadsheet. A few of those tone cases are actually important for compliance — we can't have evasive-sounding responses.
[03:20] Priya Shah: On the security side, quick notes: we need to validate support for our KMS provider (Hashicorp Vault) and SSO via SAML. Also audit logs need to show token-level request IDs for two months retention.
[03:33] Lina Torres: We have a security pack we can share; I'll attach the SOC2 docs and the KMS integration notes. Raj, can you confirm if audit log retention can be configured?
[03:42] Raj Patel: Yes we can configure retention on the private deployment; for hosted we have tiered retention and we can add a longer window as an add-on — will include details in the doc.
[03:52] Carlos Vega: Also procurement is asking for Dedicated pricing with a monthly commit number so we can compare against running ourselves on GCP.
[03:58] Lina Torres: We'll provide a pricing summary with expected unit economics given your throughput. I'll include a sample commit option and burst rules.
[04:07] Sam Liu: Back to prompts — Jenna, any more context on the canonical evaluation set?
[04:11] Jenna Morris: We're still finalizing, but I'll upload the target queries. The important thing is we need stable scoring rules: exact amount extraction, extract ID, and accept partial phrasing for scheduling.
[04:20] Raj Patel: Great. For immediate mitigation on the billing regression, plan: revert the prompt rewrite for that intent, add a fallback to the extraction model, and add a unit test to the eval harness. That should recover scores quickly.
[04:31] Jenna Morris: Sounds good. Do you have an estimate for time-to-fix?
[04:34] Raj Patel: We can push a patch and run the quick benchmark in about 48 hours; full regression run across the canonical set will be done by next Monday.
[04:42] Lina Torres: Awesome. Any other blockers?
[04:44] Priya Shah: One more: encryption at rest with our Vault keys for the private deployment and proof of deletion for deleted data. We'll need a short meeting with the security engineer to align.
[04:54] Lina Torres: I'll set that up; Raj, can you coordinate?
[04:57] Raj Patel: Yep will loop in infra.
[04:59] Jenna Morris: Ok thanks team, to recap: Lina sends prompt scoring + security docs; Raj runs quick benchmark and patches billing prompt; Jenna provides canonical queries. We'll reconvene same time next week.
[05:12] Lina Torres: Thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.
notes: Security pack + SOC2 to be shared by Lina: link TBD
Playbook options (conservative vs hybrid routing) to be added to the shared doc
